measurement.name: eager_stream_batch_cuda_event
measurement.definition: CUDA event interval around 100 sequential provider calls on one stream, divided by 100
measurement.included_caveat: eager host-submission gaps remain inside the CUDA-event interval; this is not isolated kernel or CUDA Graph timing

summary.selection_note: The website shows two stable Oxide advantages and two stable FlashInfer advantages; the complete case matrix is retained below.

raw_archive.location: external validation archive; every raw record is also embedded below

accepted_claims: The matched eager-provider harness completed 14 BF16 attention cases for Oxide Infer and FlashInfer 0.6.17 in both provider orders on the recorded GPU.
All 14 cases have provider-order median deltas at or below five percent for both providers; Oxide Infer has lower combined median latency in eight and FlashInfer in six.
Oxide Infer is 1.444x lower latency for the NHD paged-decode MHA B1 case and 1.695x lower latency for the short ragged-prefill MHA case.
FlashInfer is 2.209x lower latency for the long ragged GQA4 case and 11.510x lower latency for the long paged-prefill GQA4 case.

All FlashInfer outputs passed the independent PyTorch F32 reference limits recorded per case; the Oxide product paths are covered by the current R1 qualification record for the unchanged product source.
excluded_claims: an overall Oxide Infer or FlashInfer winner
isolated kernel duration or CUDA Graph replay performance
engine, model, TTFT, TPOT, token throughput, memory, or serving performance
performance on GPUs other than the recorded NVIDIA H20
